Market stance

An election-day reversal splits the group: Prof reads the overnight −2.5% Nasdaq futures flush that finished firmly green as efficient markets with the VIX crushed, iain reads QQQ's close near its lows under the 9EMA as more downside being the pain trade, and the tape underneath is a rotation — new highs in AAPL, MSFT, DIS and CROX while semis and memory names fall 7–20% — so four breakouts qualify today and the P/E list is a falling knife, not an entry.

  • U.S. election results, overnight Tue–Wed — Prof: Nasdaq futures down nearly 2.5% overnight, then a full reversal to firmly green with the VIX crushed; Remz: hedges came off after Election Day, which explains the violent move, and the real move may unfold Thursday and Friday
  • Enrich's 11/5 watchlist — upside: NFLX, JPM, MSTR, MSFT, DIS; downside: MU, ARM, CIEN, AMD; plus his forward-P/E list for AI-buildout names (CRDO 18x, AVGO 18x, NVDA 16.8x, CLS 13x, VST 12x, STX 11x, WDC 11x, CIFR 10x, MU 4.6x, SNDK 4.2x, SKHY 3.8x)

Market — SPY · QQQ · IWM · TLT

Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
An election-day reversal window: Wednesday's close was green across the board — SPY +1.65%, QQQ +0.97%, IWM +1.51%, TLT +0.80% — but the group's posts describe the tape underneath it, not the close. Prof supplies the tape read: Nasdaq futures down nearly 2.5% overnight, then a complete reversal to firmly green with the VIX crushed and Democrats sweeping — “a pretty damn good example of efficient markets.” iain supplies the counterweight on QQQ: buyers found resistance at the 9EMA and closed near the lows, so more downside is the pain trade until a close back above the 9EMA, and leadership is still weak. Remz supplies the mechanics: hedges came off after Election Day, which explains why the move was so violent, and the real move may unfold Thursday and Friday — stay open-minded into the end of the week. Sean posted nothing new in this window; his Nov 4, 00:52 UTC warning against shorting into the 200-day line was in yesterday's feed. Enrich supplies the split tape for Thursday: NFLX, JPM, MSTR, MSFT and DIS upside; MU, ARM, CIEN and AMD downside; plus a forward-P/E list for AI-buildout names that is cheap on paper and falling in price — CRDO 18x, AVGO 18x, NVDA 16.8x, CLS 13x, VST 12x, STX 11x, WDC 11x, CIFR 10x, MU 4.6x, SNDK 4.2x, SKHY 3.8x — and his own caveat, “cheap can always get cheaper, BUT only for so long.” iain adds the warning that buying SOXX, MU, SNDK or SKHY into declining moving averages on last week's bounce is the learning opportunity, and that AMZN at 270 after 230 three days ago is erratic, kinetic price action he will not chase. Venu supplies the two watchlists: Power Earnings Gap names DUOL, CROX, SPOT and FISV, and housing — ITB, TOL, RKT and LEN bottoming and reclaiming 200-day SMAs as the 10-year yield declines. DiCarlo supplies the long-term calls: AAOI in his Smart Money Zone buy zone with a 12–24 month target of $206, and his full APP thesis. Remz supplies the short side: SPCX short under $130, KLAC puts under $150, and his DELL short mostly covered since $448. Your process gives four clean qualifiers today — AAPL, MSFT, DIS and CROX all closed at new 52-week highs above every average — while the rest of the tape is tests to survive: NVDA on its 50-week line at 201.22, GOOGL's $270 test from yesterday, UBER a hair above its 50-day, and the entire P/E list falling 2–20% in a single session. The discipline is in the framing: breakouts to hold (AAPL 349.51, MSFT 555.80, DIS 118.95, CROX 159.84) against the downside list and iain's warning list, which are shorts and avoids, not entries.

  • Level strength: Strong = 2+ confluent anchors (52w high/low, 3m swing, 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA, trader-stated) within 0.75%, or a 52w extreme with 3+ weekly touches in the past year. Moderate = 1 anchor or 2–3 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels. KLAC and SPCX show no invalidation row: they are short ideas, and there is no long thesis below to invalidate. CLS, VST and CIFR show no invalidation row: they closed at their 52-week lows, so no lower anchor exists.
  • Trader charts: none embedded this edition. No trader posted a retrievable chart image for a covered name in the visible posts this window, so no trader chart is embedded rather than risking a wrong one.
  • Chart verification gate: every plotted line's endpoint was checked against levels.json before the HTML was built — all computable lines passed within 0.5%. The 30-week MA is a true trailing mean over full 30-week windows only.
